Yes. Pointwise convergence of polynomials on [0,1] implies uniform convergence.

Proof sketch:

1. Pointwise convergence yields pointwise boundedness: ∀ x, sup_n |B_n(x)| < ∞.

2. Banach–Steinhaus theorem (uniform boundedness principle), applied in Banach space C[0,1] with sup norm, yields uniform boundedness: ∃ M with |B_n(x)| ≤ M ∀ x, ∀ n. Key: pointwise boundedness of polynomials on [0,1] implies boundedness under every continuous linear functional on C[0,1], hence norm-boundedness by UBP.

3. Limit f is continuous. Pointwise convergence everywhere + uniform boundedness of polynomials precludes discontinuities of f.

4. Uniform boundedness + pointwise convergence to continuous limit yields uniform convergence. Polynomials are rigid: any polynomial bounded on [0,1] is controlled by values on any subinterval of positive length. Compactness argument using finite δ-cover: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N: |B_n(x) − f(x)| < ε ∀ x, n ≥ N.
